chapter: La Vida and Handy's own bands
title: Handy's Louisiana Shakers and its touring
summary: After La Vida he led a large band touring Texas, Florida, Alabama and Mississippi, and played against Celestin.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, he died here about three years ago. I think he taking Alfred's place with me at the La Vida. But after I left the La Vida, then I organized me a large band. I had the person named Hannes Louisiana Shakers. Well, I had Willie Pacho on the first trumpet. I had Rick R. Alexis on the second trumpet. I had Robert on the trombone. I had George Clark on the tenor. My cell phone alto. I had a little fella playing alto. He dropped the date up at Jackson and Germany. What was his name? I think it's his name in a minute. I had H.A. Minor on the guitar. I had Old Man Kimball on the bass. Raymond Doyce on the piano. Roy Evans on drums. No vocalists. Didn't have nobody singing. At that time, singers wasn't doing so well. Just instrument, you know. Instrument band. Singers wasn't doing so much. We did a lot of work. We worked out at Fourth Way, Texas. Beaumont. Ascended Torn. Houston. Galveston. Florida. Pensacola. Alabama. Alabama. We played a place I did called Chickasaw, Alabama. Played Mobile a lot of times. I'm Biloxi. Guffbo. Pash Christian. Place is called Franklinton out here on the other side of Bugaloosa. We played Bugaloosa over three or four times a month. We played against Celestan at the Roosevelt Hotel. After that, I lost all my music.
